subject: Renewal paperwork: ROFR clause + order form addendum redlines
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@novacorp.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@novacorp.com>, legal@novacorp.com
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal packet + ROFR question

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning — Novacorp is aligned to move forward with the 18-month renewal and the proposed 20% capacity uplift. Our legal team attached the redlines to the order form and a short note about a contractual request: Novacorp would like a Right of First Refusal (ROFR) for any price/term changes that would affect their committed capacity during the term.

I've attached our annotated PDF (Novacorp_redlines_v1.pdf). High level asks:
- Add ROFR language in the Order Form Addendum (section 4) to allow Novacorp a 14-day window to match any materially different offer Redwood provides to other customers for similar committed capacity tiers.
- Clarify billing proration for mid-term capacity increases and whether the committed rates can be rebalanced mid-term.
- Update Exhibit C to reflect the new usage tiers and footprint.

Can we get Redwood legal to review and confirm any changes to MSA exposure (indemnity/term/termination) if we add a ROFR? Daniel and I copied procurement/legal on the thread.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — Novacorp is aiming to get paperwork signed by Oct 15.

Best,
Emily

Attachment: Novacorp_redlines_v1.pdf (annotated)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@novacorp.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal packet + ROFR question

Emily — thanks for the note and for sending the annotated PDF. I reviewed the high-level asks with Monica and Karthik. Quick responses up front:

- We can support a limited ROFR for committed capacity tiers, but we need to scope it narrowly to avoid broad resale constraints. Proposed carve: ROFR applies only to identical committed capacity bundles and pricing for the same region and term length. 14-day window seems reasonable operationally.
- Billing proration: we typically prorate mid-term capacity increases from the effective date of the addendum. We'll confirm language in the addendum to make that explicit.
- Exhibit C: we'll sync to ensure the usage tiers match the technical footprint and that there are no unexpected SLAs changes.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood legal (Laura) will produce a tracked-change Order Form Addendum and an MSA excerpt showing ROFR language + guardrails.
2) We'll post a draft to the Drive link and send a DocuSign when internal legal signs off.
3) Monica will coordinate with CS on migration/onboarding timeline for the added capacity.

Karthik — can you take point on commercial language (ROFR carve + pricing fallbacks)? Laura — can legal provide a redline by EOD tomorrow so Novacorp legal can review?

Matt (cc: internal) — tagging for awareness.

Thanks,
Mateo
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: emily.chen@novacorp.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, legal@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal packet + ROFR question

Emily / Daniel / team —

Thanks for sending the annotated file. I've attached an internal draft (RI_OrderForm_Addendum_draft.docx) with tracked changes that implement a narrow ROFR and clarify the proration mechanics. Key legal guardrails included:

- ROFR limited to: 
  * identical committed capacity bundles (by SKU and region),
  * same term length or longer,
  * and only where Redwood enters a separate commercial agreement with third parties that would materially change price or contractual terms for the bundle.
- Exclusions: renewals of legacy customers who migrate to equivalent bundles under agreed migration programs; reseller deals that do not change net customer price.
- A 14-calendar-day notice window for Novacorp to elect to match the material terms; Redwood must provide written notice with the material terms and the offered time window.
- We added a short clause preserving Redwood's right to offer promotions publicly (e.g., general limited-time discounts) without triggering ROFR unless the promotion is targeted to specific named accounts in a way that would apply to the same committed bundle.

Regarding MSA exposure: the ROFR carve is contractual rather than creating a service-level or indemnity obligation. There is modest operational exposure (notice timing) but nothing we see that requires changing core indemnities or term/termination rights. We did not add any new SLA obligations.

Please review the attached draft and let us know whether Novacorp legal is comfortable with the narrowness of the carve and the exclusions. If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute legal-to-legal call tomorrow to walk through tracked changes.

Attachment: RI_OrderForm_Addendum_draft.docx

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@novacorp.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, emily.chen@novacorp.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, legal@novacorp.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal packet + ROFR question

Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear draft. A few points from Novacorp legal that we want clarified in redline before internal approval:

1) The definition of "identical committed capacity bundle" — can we add a short table in Exhibit C that maps SKU codes to the bundle definition so there is no ambiguity?
2) Proration formula — Novacorp procurement prefers a per-day proration basis with the effective date tied to the DocuSign execution date. Can Redwood confirm that's acceptable?
3) The exclusion for promotions is good, but can we add an auditability clause so Novacorp can request the notice and supporting terms that triggered a ROFR offer (redacted commercially sensitive information OK).

If you can incorporate these three items into the tracked changes we can circulate for sign-off. We remain on schedule for Oct 15 but would like to lock final redlines by Oct 12.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Procurement — Novacorp

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: daniel.brooks@novacorp.com, emily.chen@novacorp.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal packet + ROFR question

Daniel / Emily — appreciate the feedback. Quick update on changes we just uploaded to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNOVACORP-RENEWAL

What we changed in the latest draft (tracked):
- Exhibit C: added a mapping table of SKU -> bundle name -> region -> committed units (per your request). That should make "identical bundle" concrete.
- Proration: we've clarified proration on a per-day basis and tied the effective date to the date of DocuSign execution (we added language that the effective date is the signature date unless otherwise agreed in writing).
- Auditability: added a short provision allowing Novacorp to request the notice and supporting terms that triggered the ROFR; Redwood will provide a redacted copy of the material terms within seven business days. This is limited to non-sensitive commercial info and excludes provider pricing models.

I will have our team prepare the final tracked PDF and a DocuSign envelope (https://secure.redwood.com/docusign/ABC123). We expect internal legal + commercial approvals from our side by EOD today.

Action items / timeline:
- Novacorp legal to review the Drive draft and confirm or provide final redline by Oct 12 EOD.
- Redwood to issue DocuSign after sign-off.
- Monica to confirm onboarding window and start dates once signed.

If helpful, Laura and I can hop on a 20-minute call Monday morning to close any last language.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
